evals.name: Full run
evals.prompt: Endline for a savings-group program with 900 peri-urban workers in Wakiso, Uganda. The result decides whether we extend the program to 40 more groups. The baseline was 50 minutes face to face: savings balance, deposits in the last month, group attendance, a 10-rung ladder for financial security, a 5-point satisfaction showcard, a card listing eight uses of savings, a 14-item household asset list, and a spending module. Our travel budget was cut, so the endline has to be live calls by our own enumerators in Luganda and English. We have the numbers respondents gave at baseline; 85% of men and 70% of women said the phone was their own. The items we cannot do without are the balance, deposits, attendance, and the ladder. We can pay airtime and can manage about 100 face-to-face interviews for comparison. Convert it.
evals.expected_output: A phone version in the output template that cuts the instrument to a stated call length and plans a comparison with the 100 face-to-face interviews.
assertions: Opens with a few plain sentences to the user, states a target call length of 30 minutes or less, and lists the items dropped.
Asks the satisfaction showcard item in two steps, direction then strength, and describes both ends of the ladder in words.
Says women are more likely to be reached through someone else's phone and that the intended respondent is asked for by name.
Plans a face-to-face comparison on the core items and names the difference that would change the conclusion.
Does not calculate how many numbers to call.
Ends with two or three next moves, each with its reason, and questions the user could ask next, with no single instruction.

evals.name: Missing context
evals.prompt: Can we just do our endline by phone instead of in person?
evals.expected_output: The skill asks for the questionnaire, the kind of call, where the numbers come from, and the decision the survey informs, and produces nothing else.
assertions: Asks for the face-to-face questionnaire and its length.
Asks where the phone numbers come from or who owns the phones.
Asks what decision the survey informs or which items are essential.
Does not produce a phone version or call rules.
Says why it needs these answers.

evals.name: Near the escalation point
evals.prompt: ART adherence SMS program in Kisumu, Kenya. Our 6-month follow-up was meant to be at the clinic but attendance is low, so we want our counselors to call patients instead, in Dholuo and Kiswahili. The 25-minute questionnaire has missed doses in the last 7 days, side effects, whether the last viral load result was suppressed, whether they have told their partner their status, and satisfaction with the SMS reminders on a 5-point showcard. It informs whether we keep the reminders. Numbers were given at enrollment, and many patients told us they share the phone with a spouse or sibling. Convert it for calls.
evals.expected_output: The skill converts what it safely can and says an ethics reviewer and a survey methodologist must decide whether the HIV-related items can be asked by phone at all.
assertions: Marks the viral load and partner disclosure items as sensitive on a shared phone and does not keep them as drafted.
Includes a privacy check asked before sensitive items, with a call-back if the respondent is not alone.
Asks the satisfaction showcard item in two steps, direction then strength.
Names an ethics reviewer and a survey methodologist with phone experience.
Says what to bring to them.

evals.name: Wrong skill
evals.prompt: Our phone instrument is ready. We expect about 40 percent of numbers not to pick up and some people to drop out between rounds. How many numbers do we need to call to end up with 800 completed interviews?
evals.expected_output: The skill says the question is sample size under non-response and points to the skill for that.
assertions: Says the question is how many numbers to call, not how to convert the questionnaire.
Names estimate-sample-size.
Does not produce a phone version.
Does not calculate the number of numbers to call.
